nodes.title: How Much Protein Per Meal (TODAY.com)
nodes.claim: Dietitians tell readers to eat 20-30 g protein per meal (20-40 g if goals are higher), saying the body 'can only absorb and use a certain amount of protein at a time,' the cap is 'up for debate... some research saying 30 grams and other studies saying 40 grams,' and there is 'no reason to eat more than 40 grams at once.'
nodes.note: Most viral mainstream restatement: turns an MPS plateau into a digestive absorb-and-excrete ceiling.

nodes.title: Eat to Build Muscle: Every 3 Hours, 30 g
nodes.claim: Recommends eating every ~3 hours across six meals a day and to 'shoot for about 30 grams of protein per meal' to support muscle growth.
nodes.note: Canonical gym-lore pairing: the 3-hour meal cadence plus a 30 g per-meal cap.

nodes.title: r/ScientificNutrition: Only 20-30 g Absorbed?
nodes.claim: Thread opens with the premise 'If a person can only absorb 20 or 30 grams of protein a time' and asks how bulk eating is even possible - the ceiling repeated as settled fact before debate begins.
nodes.note: The myth as crowdsourced common sense; thread title is itself the mutated claim.

nodes.title: How Much Protein Do You Need Daily? (UnityPoint)
nodes.claim: A dietitian advises metabolizing protein '15-30 grams at a time' because 'studies show a higher intake of protein, like more than 40 grams in one sitting, isn't more beneficial.'
nodes.note: Institutional health authority laundering the ceiling into clinical-sounding guidance.

nodes.title: Protein Dose Response of MPS After Resistance Exercise
nodes.authors: Moore DR et al. (Am J Clin Nutr)
nodes.claim: In 6 young men after leg-only resistance exercise, 20 g whole-egg protein maximally stimulated muscle protein synthesis; 40 g produced no statistically significant further rise (a small ~10-20% bump) but did increase leucine oxidation.
nodes.note: The misread anchor: a leg-exercise MPS plateau in 6 subjects that nobody citing a '30-40 g digestive ceiling' represents faithfully.

nodes.title: How Much Protein Can the Body Use in a Single Meal?
nodes.authors: Schoenfeld BJ & Aragon AA (J Int Soc Sports Nutr)
nodes.claim: Recommends 0.4 g/kg/meal across at least 4 meals (>=1.6 g/kg/day) and argues higher per-meal doses are not all oxidized - explicitly rejecting a hard single-meal utilization ceiling.
nodes.note: The corrective review that keeps the per-meal framing but demolishes the absolute cap.

nodes.title: 40 g vs 20 g Whey After Whole-Body Exercise
nodes.claim: In 30 resistance-trained men after whole-body resistance exercise, 40 g whey stimulated greater muscle protein synthesis than 20 g (0.059 vs 0.049 %/h, P=0.005).
nodes.note: Direct counter-evidence: doubles the 'max useful dose' once whole-body training is used.

nodes.title: 30 g vs 90 g Lean Beef and MPS
nodes.authors: Symons TB et al. (J Am Diet Assoc)
nodes.claim: A 113 g beef serving (30 g protein) raised muscle protein synthesis ~50% in young and elderly adults; a 340 g serving (90 g protein) produced no further increase over 5 h.
nodes.note: The honest nuance the myth omits: a real plateau over 5 h, but for MPS - not an absorption ceiling.

nodes.title: ISSN Position Stand: Protein and Exercise
nodes.authors: Jäger R et al. (J Int Soc Sports Nutr)
nodes.claim: Position stand recommends 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day for most exercising individuals and frames per-meal doses of ~20-40 g as context-dependent rather than a fixed absorption limit.
nodes.note: Society-level synthesis the pop layer never quotes.

nodes.title: How Much Protein Can You Eat in One Sitting?
nodes.claim: Reviews the dose-response literature (Moore 2009, Symons 2009, Macnaughton 2016) and concludes the body can absorb and use well more than 30 g in one sitting - the '30 g max' is a misreading of acute MPS studies.
nodes.note: Lay-friendly debunk the mutated layer ignores; live page bot-blocked during verification (URL real, archived Jan 2025).

nodes.title: No Upper Limit to the Anabolic Response (100 g vs 25 g)
nodes.authors: Trommelen J et al. (Cell Rep Med)
nodes.claim: 100 g milk protein produced a greater and more prolonged (>12 h) anabolic response than 25 g, with amino-acid incorporation rising dose-dependently - the response had 'no upper limit in magnitude and duration' in vivo in humans.
nodes.note: The lonely, ignored endpoint: the only node cited by none of the popular chain - four times the 'max' and the curve was still climbing.
